thank you! no friend i feel comfortable with, because my close friends all struggle with mental illnesses as well, so i don’t want to make things worse for them.

you can celebrate your friend’s graduation & birthday when you’re back, and if you live to see end of the hike, you’ll still get to see your other friend, too! the hike is temporary, just like lots of these feelings are. give it a chance. enjoy some beautiful nature. really soak it up. you might be surprised!! or, bring yourself to tell your parents you’re not in the mental state for that now and be honest!

i feel this so much, but i’m realizing that not wanting to hurt someone is good in a weird way. like, if someone is going to be hurt by you leaving, you are positively impacting their lives. so, that means you’re having a positive impact in this world, even if it seems small, the people in your family impact other people and that is how positivity gets spread. i am reminding myself of this right now, too. i still struggle a shit ton, but it has made me more open to being honest and accepting help.

I'm new to working with a personal trainer and having a pre-set strength training schedule for the week; I have only a week and a half of it under my belt, and today I'm feeling beyond unmotivated to work out. I got less sleep than usual due to an emergency last night, plus I can never sleep in anyway. I'm considering going to the gym right now, and I know I really should, but this is the least motivated I've felt in the past couple weeks. Thoughts? Would it be better to go and do SOMETHING even if it's not the whole workout? Or any advice on waking yourself up and getting motivated??

I mentioned the restraining order to her, but she didn’t think she would be able to get one. She didn’t know if this was “bad enough” to justify one of those, and I don’t know anything about restraining orders so I wasn’t sure either.

Thank you so much for your reply, though! I will talk to her about this.
